 I have, I think, two full horizon permution tables with alphabet sizes of 31 and 42. Not as strong in terms of alphabet size as @helmeden 26 alphabet witness, but these cover the isomorphs pt equalities much more correctly, i.e. the 15 patterns with max = 100 and min = 3 and 18 patterns with min = 2 respectively, Shared Sections yes, Extend no, Remove Redundant yes. With a minimal unlink for the weird 26-card isomorph (E4:pos68 unlinked in every pattern that contains it). Those alphabet sizes are the lowest I could do, but it's not a proven lower bound. In fact even at these sizes there are probably multiple solutions that cover the 15 pattern set, I've found two 31 solutions but nothing lower than that. The 42 solution is even more of a compute wall. (Still ordinary gack with identity shared starting decks.)
